question.leadin: This leader edited the Ems Dispatch, helping to start a war with France.
question.text: Name this man whose use of Realpolitik earned him the nickname the "Iron Chancellor."
question.clue: This leader stated that the great questions of the day would be decided by "Blood and Iron".

swap.text: Merkel belongs to this German political party, which is mainly opposed by the Social Democratic Party.
swap.clue: This party's leaders Ludwig Erhard and Konrad Adenauer sparked an "economic miracle" in its country post-World War II, and it has participated in various "Grand Coalitions" with the Social Democratic Party.

question.leadin: This country's first Chancellor, Konrad Adenauer (AH-den-ow-er), presided over its economic miracle, which is also called Wirtschaftswunder (veer-CHAHFTS-voonder) or the Miracle on the Rhine.
question.text: Name this country which was part of the Western Bloc during the Cold War. Willy Brandt, a leader of this country, championed its philosophy of Ostpolitik which sought to normalize relations with its eastern neighbor.
question.answerHtml: West Germany [accept Federal Republic of Germany or FRG or BRD or Bonn Republic; prompt on Germany; do not accept or prompt on “East Germany” or “German Democratic Republic” or “GDR” or “DDR”]
question.clue: One leader of this country was forced to resign after his aide Gunter Guillaume was revealed to be a spy.

swap.leadin: Name these high ranking Nazi officials.
swap.text: This head of the German Navy became leader of the Third Reich following Hitler's suicide and ordered the German surrender that ended World War II in Europe.
swap.clue: Following Hitler's suicide, this admiral served for nearly a month as president of Germany in a government with Chancellor Goebbels ].

question.text: Along with Erich Ludendorff, Hitler earlier had tried to lead this failed 1923 uprising in Munich. It ended with his arrest, and while in jail, he published Mein Kampf.
question.clue: Its leader started it with the proclamation that "The National Revolution has begun" and this event ended after a brief firefight between insurgents and police in the Residenzstrasse.

swap.leadin: Its failure at the First Battle of the Marne led to the "Race to the Sea"
swap.text: Name this plan that was devised by Germany prior to WWI to fight a two front war against France and Russia. It called for German forces to sweep counterclockwise through Belgium, the Netherlands, and Luxemburg into France.
swap.clue: This German strategy, named for a former German field marshal, advocated sweeping through France, then transporting troops east to handle the slower-to-mobilize Russian forces.

question.leadin: As a result of this event, Hermann Goring committed suicide.
question.text: Name this set of tribunals, held in a namesake Bavarian city, during which Rudolf Hess and other leaders of a defeated government were prosecuted for crimes against humanity.
question.clue: Robert Ley committed suicide before the conclusion of this event, which was held at the Palace of Justice.

swap.text: In response to the Catholic Church's opposition to Prussia in wars such as the Franco-Prussian War, Bismarck promulgated an effort given this name, coined by Rudolph Virchow.
swap.clue: This social conflict came to an end with the passage of the First Mitigation Law negotiated following the death of Pius IX ], allowing clerics to be exempt from some Prussian laws.

question.text: John George I ("the first"), the ruler of this state, was forced to ally with Gustavus Adolphus after his lands were invaded by Tilly shortly before Breitenfeld.
question.clue: During World War I, George V renamed a royal house named for this region, Coburg, and Gotha to the House of Windsor.

swap.text: Rohm and his SA were eliminated in this event, which saw killings carried out by the Gestapo and SS. It also names an Arthurian event, and Harold Macmillan's dismissal of members of his cabinet. Also called Operation Hummingbird, it is named for a certain weapon.
swap.clue: Upon his release, Vice-Chancellor von Papen's criticism of the regime was silenced.

question.text: This steel company, founded in the Ruhr, produced most German weapons in both World Wars. It merged with Thyssen ("TISS-in") in 1999 and is a major producer of elevators, among other products.
question.clue: This family adopted a symbol of three interlocking rings after it gained dominance of the railway wheel market in the 1850s. The Langer Max was one of the products built in this family's factories in Essen.

swap.text: The Battle of Koniggratz was a skirmish in this larger conflict, sometimes called the Seven Weeks War. The ostensible cause of this conflict was the Schleswig-Holstein problem.
swap.clue: Either Koniggratz or Sadowa was the most important battle in this war, a decisive victory for the northern belligerents.

question.text: Barnstormers often performed in groups called Flying Circuses. This nobleman led a fighter pilot squadron in World War I nicknamed the Flying Circus.
question.answerHtml: Manfred von Richthofen [or Manfred Albrecht Freiherr von Richthofen; or the Red Baron]
question.clue: His 80 kills led all aces during war, though he did not survive it; his famed red Fokker triplane was downed in April 1918, with both Australian anti-aircraft gunners and Canadian pilot Roy Brown claiming credit.

swap.leadin: After his capture, this man supposedly proclaimed that he fought for Omnia Sunt Communia, the principle of redistributing wealth so all would be in common, leading some historians to see his struggle as a precursor to communism.
swap.text: Name this preacher who played a leading role during the German Peasants' War until his capture after the Battle of Frankenhausen.
swap.clue: This religious leader ministered to the weaver Nicholas Storch as well as two other members of a group of Anabaptist lay preachers called the Zwickau (TZVIH-"cow") Prophets.

question.text: The secular electors included the margrave of this northeastern German state, which merged into Prussia in the 1600s.
question.clue: The portion of this polity east of the Oder-Neisse line is the Neumark, which was transferred to Poland following World War II.

swap.leadin: Answer the following questions about the career of German statesman Otto von Bismarck.
swap.text: In a notable 1862 speech, Bismarck famously declared that "not through speeches and majority decisions will the great questions of the day be decided", but instead by means of these two substances.
swap.clue: It was given during a constitutional crisis triggered by bills on military expenditures introduced by the king.

question.text: Skorzeny was supposed to head this mythically-named program to conduct irregular warfare post-1945. Instead, he helped set up the related ODESSA network to help Nazis escape.
question.clue: This underground partisan network set up by the SS to resist the Allied occupation of Nazi Germany.

swap.leadin: This man had little success in convincing the Catholic Church to act upon his namesake report.
swap.text: Identify this man who helped deliver Zyklon B to concentration camps, but who also attempted to pass on details about the horrors of the Holocaust to men such as Goran von Otter. He's a character in William T. Vollmann's novel, Europe Central.
swap.clue: This SS Officer assigned to the Hygiene Institute and charged with delivering Zyklon B wrote a report of what he witnessed in that time at camps like Belzec. He reportedly attempted to communicate the info to the Allies through a Swede named Goran van Otter.

question.leadin: Willibald claimed that Saint Boniface took this inflammatory action before constructing a church dedicated to Saint Peter.
question.text: Describe this symbolic action done to end a decades-long conflict to forcibly christianize a people who lived northeast of Austrasia under their leader Widukind.
question.answerHtml: chopping down a sacred tree [accept answers like chopping down the Irminsul, cutting down Donar’s Oak, or removing a stump; prompt on chopping down, cutting, removing, or similar answers by asking “to what object”]

swap.leadin: Answer the following about a certain dynasty FTPE.
swap.text: Divided between its Swabian and Franconian lines, this dynasty ascended to power when Emperor Sigismund named Frederick I the Elector of Brandenburg.
swap.clue: Its Franconian line took control of the margraviates of Ansbach and Kulmbach, and, with the extinction of its Hechingen branch, Charles Anton of its Sigmaringen line took the title of Furst.
